pearson_correlation.description: Calculate Pearson correlation coefficient between two numerical variables
pearson_correlation.implementation:
1. Calculate mean of x and y
2. Calculate covariance: sum((x - mean_x) * (y - mean_y)) / (n-1)
3. Calculate standard deviations of x and y
4. Correlation = covariance / (std_x * std_y)
5. Calculate p-value using t-distribution with n-2 degrees of freedom
6. Return JSON: {"correlation": value, "p_value": value}

spearman_correlation.implementation:
1. Convert x and y to ranks
2. Calculate Pearson correlation on ranks
3. Calculate p-value using t-distribution
4. Return JSON: {"correlation": value, "p_value": value}

linear_regression.implementation:
1. Calculate mean of x and y
2. Calculate slope: sum((x - mean_x) * (y - mean_y)) / sum((x - mean_x)^2)
3. Calculate intercept: mean_y - slope * mean_x
4. Calculate R-squared: 1 - (sum((y - predicted)^2) / sum((y - mean_y)^2))
5. Calculate standard error of regression
6. Calculate p-values for coefficients using t-distribution
7. Return JSON: {"slope": value, "intercept": value, "r_squared": value, "std_error": value, "p_value": value}

t_test.implementation:
1. Calculate means of both groups
2. Calculate pooled standard deviation
3. Calculate t-statistic: (mean1 - mean2) / (pooled_std * sqrt(1/n1 + 1/n2))
4. Calculate degrees of freedom: n1 + n2 - 2
5. Calculate p-value using t-distribution
6. Return JSON: {"t_statistic": value, "p_value": value, "df": value}

anova.implementation:
1. Calculate overall mean
2. Calculate between-group sum of squares
3. Calculate within-group sum of squares
4. Calculate F-statistic: (between_SS/df_between) / (within_SS/df_within)
5. Calculate p-value using F-distribution
6. Return JSON: {"f_statistic": value, "p_value": value, "df_between": value, "df_within": value}

chi_square_test.implementation:
1. Create contingency table
2. Calculate expected frequencies
3. Calculate chi-square statistic: sum((observed - expected)^2 / expected)
4. Calculate degrees of freedom: (rows-1) * (cols-1)
5. Calculate p-value using chi-square distribution
6. Return JSON: {"chi_square": value, "p_value": value, "df": value}

descriptive_stats.description: Calculate descriptive statistics for numerical data
descriptive_stats.implementation:
1. Calculate mean
2. Calculate median
3. Calculate standard deviation
4. Calculate quartiles (Q1, Q2, Q3)
5. Calculate minimum and maximum
6. Return JSON: {"mean": value, "median": value, "std": value, "q1": value, "q3": value, "min": value, "max": value}

frequency_analysis.description: Perform frequency analysis for categorical data
frequency_analysis.implementation:
1. Count frequency of each category
2. Calculate percentage of each category
3. Calculate cumulative frequency
4. Return JSON: {"frequencies": {"category1": count1, "category2": count2}, "percentages": {"category1": pct1, "category2": pct2}}

mann_whitney_u.description: Perform Mann-Whitney U test for comparing two independent samples
mann_whitney_u.implementation: 1. Rank all the values from both groups together. 2. Calculate the sum of ranks for each group. 3. Use the Mann-Whitney U formula to compute U-statistic. 4. Calculate the p-value using U and sample sizes. 5. Return JSON: {"u_statistic": value, "p_value": value}

fishers_exact_test.description: Perform Fisher's exact test for small-sample categorical data
fishers_exact_test.implementation: 1. Construct a 2x2 contingency table. 2. Calculate the exact p-value for independence. 3. Return JSON: {"p_value": value, "odds_ratio": value}

count.description: Count the number of non-missing values in the data
count.implementation: 1. Remove missing values from the data. 2. Count the number of remaining values. 3. Return JSON: {"count": value}

minimum.description: Find the minimum value in the data
minimum.implementation: 1. Remove missing values from the data. 2. Identify the smallest value. 3. Return JSON: {"minimum": value}

maximum.description: Find the maximum value in the data
maximum.implementation: 1. Remove missing values from the data. 2. Identify the largest value. 3. Return JSON: {"maximum": value}

quartiles.description: Calculate the first (Q1), second (Q2, median), and third (Q3) quartiles of the data
quartiles.implementation: 1. Remove missing values from the data. 2. Sort the data in ascending order. 3. Calculate Q1 (25th percentile), Q2 (50th percentile, median), and Q3 (75th percentile). 4. Return JSON: {"q1": value, "q2": value, "q3": value}

IQR.description: Calculate the interquartile range (IQR) of the data
IQR.implementation: 1. Remove missing values from the data. 2. Calculate Q1 (25th percentile) and Q3 (75th percentile). 3. Compute IQR = Q3 - Q1. 4. Return JSON: {"iqr": value}

skewness.description: Calculate the skewness of the data distribution
skewness.implementation: 1. Remove missing values from the data. 2. Calculate the mean and standard deviation. 3. Compute skewness using the formula: skewness = (1/n) * sum(((x_i - mean)/std)^3). 4. Return JSON: {"skewness": value}

kurtosis.description: Calculate the kurtosis of the data distribution
kurtosis.implementation: 1. Remove missing values from the data. 2. Calculate the mean and standard deviation. 3. Compute kurtosis using the formula: kurtosis = (1/n) * sum(((x_i - mean)/std)^4) - 3. 4. Return JSON: {"kurtosis": value}

frequency.description: Calculates the frequency of each unique value in a categorical dataset.
frequency.implementation: Count the occurrences of each unique value in the provided data. Return the counts for each category.
frequency.returns: A JSON object with results and interpretation.

mode.description: Calculates the mode(s) of a dataset.
mode.implementation: Find the value(s) that appear most frequently in the data. It is possible to have one or more modes.
mode.returns: A JSON object with the mode(s) and interpretation.

cramers_v.description: Calculates Cramér's V to measure the association between two categorical variables.
cramers_v.implementation: 1. Calculate the Chi-Square statistic. 2. Calculate Cramér's V using the formula: V = sqrt(chi_square / (n * (min(k, r) - 1))), where n is the total number of observations, k is the number of columns, and r is the number of rows. 3. Return the value of Cramér's V and its interpretation.
cramers_v.returns: A JSON object with the Cramér's V statistic and interpretation.
